children: Pilot facility will use surplus solar power to produce hydrogen for manufacturing operations, with wider adoption planned across Haryana and Gujarat

Maruti Suzuki India has commissioned a 300 kilowatt (kW) green hydrogen electrolyser plant at its Manesar manufacturing facility in Haryana, marking the company’s first such pilot project. The hydrogen produced will be blended with natural gas and used as process fuel in manufacturing operations.

The project is designed to make use of solar energy generated at the Manesar facility during holidays, when part of the electricity would otherwise remain unused. The surplus solar power is used to produce green hydrogen, which is then stored for use in manufacturing operations.

Maruti Suzuki said the pilot will help the company assess the use of green hydrogen as part of its manufacturing energy mix. Based on the learnings from the project, the automaker plans to scale up green hydrogen technology across its manufacturing facilities in Haryana and Gujarat.
The green hydrogen initiative is being implemented alongside the company’s expansion of solar power, biogas and battery energy storage systems.

Maruti Suzuki is also developing a 10 tonnes per day biogas plant at its Kharkhoda facility, which is scheduled for commissioning during FY 2026-27. The company has commissioned a 1 megawatt-hour battery energy storage system at the same facility.
The automaker has also started using compressed biogas (CBG) as a process fuel. Its board has approved four CBG projects with a combined allocation of Rs 561 crore.

The company aims to reduce the carbon footprint of its manufacturing operations from 6,15,000 tonnes currently to 2,66,000 tonnes by FY 2030-31. The company said this target will be pursued through a combination of clean-energy technologies rather than green hydrogen alone.
